title: Stochastic and Deterministic Models of the Eradication of Ebola in West Africa

limitations: All 25 rendered pages reviewed through three contact sheets.
OCR damages Greek symbols and bullet glyphs; rendered diagrams/equations are authoritative.
The paper uses fitted K/T values, short WHO window, and an unpriced treatment-efficiency proxy.

task_reconstruction.source: Summary, Introduction, Mathematical Models, Validation, Improved Treatment, Fixed Point analysis, Conclusion, and WMA letter
deliverables: Build stochastic and deterministic three-state Ebola models.
Estimate rates and initial states from WHO/population data.
Validate both model classes against the 85-day WHO window.
Compare medical services, medicine, and vaccination at six-month, one-year, two-year, and long-term horizons.
Derive fixed-point/Jury conditions for stable eradication and translate findings to WMA recommendations.
task_reconstruction.reconstruction_limit: No separate official problem statement was located; the author-defined problem approach and path-derived A label are retained without content-based reclassification.

contributions.summary: An eight-transition graph connects infected, vulnerable, and immune states.
Random event probabilities generate integer trajectories and counters.
Daily recurrences support analytical fixed-point and stability work.
WHO and population tables produce initial/rate parameters.
Three intervention mechanisms map to alpha, beta/gamma, and nu.
Case 6 and Jury analysis reduce to a vaccination threshold.

assumptions.summary: The outbreak is confined to Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.
Net migration is zero and birth/death rates are constant.
States are binary and instantaneous; population is homogeneous.
No mutation, complete recovery immunity, living-person transmission proxy, and infection-independent recovery/death.
Treatment practices remain constant over the WHO calibration window.
Unreported recovery is neglected, H0=0, and I0 is cases minus deaths.
Death reduction per percentage treatment change proxies efficiency because cost data are absent.
Case 6 and asymptotic population assumptions support the vaccination threshold.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: CountryMeters population, birth, and death counts become epsilon/delta and initial population.
Cases/deaths become I0 and P0 under explicit recovered-case caveat.
Mortality, residence time T, and K map to gamma, beta, and alpha.
WHO endpoint cases/deaths and standard deviations define error checks.

models.summary: Eight transitions over three population states.
Event probabilities and cumulative random selection.
Replicated endpoint and indirect deterministic validation.

verification.summary: Ten-run average and standard deviation compared with WHO.
Deterministic endpoints compared with stochastic states.
Jury inequality is substituted and reduced.

results_trace.summary: Five of eight statistics lie within half a standard deviation and none exceed 1.1 SD.
Medicine and services dominate short term; vaccination becomes more competitive medium term.
Current treatment produces delayed growth and motivates fixed-point analysis.
Under Case 6 and asymptotic assumptions, nu > 1-delta.

writing_logic.summary: Scope -> state abstraction -> validation -> forecast -> interventions -> horizons -> WMA.
Roadmap -> problem approach -> intervention list -> data-limited scope.
Stochastic event process -> deterministic recurrence -> role assignment.
Source tables -> equations -> initial states -> fitted parameters.
Replicates -> endpoint errors -> residual explanation -> indirect deterministic check.
Baseline -> parameter perturbation -> horizon simulations -> efficiency proxy.
Simulation trend -> fixed-point enumeration -> Jury algebra -> threshold.
Strengths -> weaknesses -> future work -> extension -> conclusion.
Model evidence -> country/horizon recommendations -> cost caveat.

language_observations.summary: The abstract repeats scope, validation, horizons, and stakeholder handoff in compressed form.
The state graph is followed by a numbered rate table and prose definition.
Horizon-specific recommendation is immediately bounded by omitted cost data.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A replicable endpoint comparison and explicit residual explanation may aid auditability; award status is not causal evidence.

weaknesses.summary: K/T are fitted to WHO and T may be a model artifact.
The 85-day window is short and WHO reporting dates/undercount limit fit claims.
Deterministic validation is indirect through stochastic agreement.
Efficiency omits cost, capacity, and interaction effects.

independent_extensions.summary: Add time-varying rates, incubation/recovery/deceased states, and waning immunity while auditing fixed-point explosion.
Add explicit cost, capacity, adherence, and joint-treatment constraints before policy ranking.

unresolved_questions: Random seed, timestep selection, and complete Matlab implementation are not reported.
K and T are fitted to a short WHO window and T is acknowledged as potentially artifactual.
WHO reporting irregularity and undercount weaken endpoint validation.
Initial recovered cases are ignored and H0 is set to zero.
Treatment efficiency is a death-reduction proxy without monetary cost, delivery capacity, or interactions.
Fixed-point/Jury derivation is model-conditional and lacks numerical eigenvalue regression.
The vaccination threshold ignores waning immunity, feasibility, and finite-population delivery.
